introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0580 Physics 1, June 2026, Ordinary Level, GCE Board, 1 h 30 min). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Where it is needed, the question itself gives the value of g ($g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$).
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section 1 (questions 1-42) has independent questions; Section 2 (questions 43-50) has two groups of questions about a practical situation (Questions 43-46 and 47-50).

Four graphs of acceleration a against force F, labelled A to D: A straight line through the origin, B decreasing straight line, C decreasing curve, D rising curve of increasing slope (Question 24).

questions.enonce_markdown: The unit of temperature is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The SI base units are the metre (length), the kilogram (mass), the second (time), the ampere (electric current), the kelvin (thermodynamic temperature), the mole and the candela. So the SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K); the ampere measures current, the kilogram mass and the metre length. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which set of energy resources below are all renewable?
questions.corrige_markdown: A renewable resource is replaced naturally as fast as it is used. Tidal and solar energy are both renewable. Nuclear fuel (uranium), coal and fossil fuels are used up and not replaced on a human time scale, so options A, C and D each contain a non-renewable resource. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A device that converts mechanical energy to electrical energy is:
questions.corrige_markdown: An a.c. generator (alternator) turns a coil in a magnetic field: mechanical (kinetic) energy becomes electrical energy by electromagnetic induction. A battery converts chemical energy, a loud speaker converts electrical energy to sound, and a microphone converts sound energy to an electrical signal (it does not produce useful electrical power from mechanical work). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.corrige_markdown: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Velocity is speed in a stated direction, so it is a vector. Mass, time and speed have magnitude only and are scalars. The usual trap is to confuse speed (scalar) with velocity (vector). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: On the celsius temperature scale $300\ K$ is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $\theta(^\circ\mathrm{C}) = T(\mathrm{K}) - 273$, so $\theta = 300 - 273 = 27\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Option B adds 273 instead of subtracting it, and option C is the conversion constant itself. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A bulldozer's broad tyres stop it from sinking too far into the soil because the broad tyres:
questions.corrige_markdown: The force on the soil is the weight of the bulldozer, which does not change with the width of the tyres (so B is false). Pressure $= \dfrac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}$: broad tyres have a larger contact area, so the same weight produces a smaller pressure and the soil is not pushed in so far. Friction does not depend on the contact area to a first approximation. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: reduce the pressure acting on the soil.
reduce the force acting on the soil.
increase the static friction acting on the soil.
increase the dynamic friction acting on the soil.

questions.enonce_markdown: A rectangular block of weight $300\ N$ has sides with areas $0.4\ m^2$ and $0.6\ m^2$. The minimum pressure the block can exert on the ground is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Pressure $= \dfrac{F}{A}$, so the pressure is smallest when the area in contact with the ground is largest. The force is the weight, $F = 300\ \mathrm{N}$, and the largest area is $0.6\ \mathrm{m^2}$: $p_{min} = \dfrac{300}{0.6} = 500\ \mathrm{Pa}$. The value 750 Pa ($300 \div 0.4$) is the maximum pressure. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the hydraulic jack that is often used to lift vehicles:
questions.corrige_markdown: A hydraulic jack works because a liquid is almost incompressible and transmits **pressure** equally in all directions (Pascal's principle). The force is not the same everywhere: it is $F = pA$, larger on the bigger piston, so C is false. To lift a heavy load with a small effort the output (load) cylinder must be larger than the input cylinder, so A and B are false. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the output cylinder has the same size as the input cylinder
the output cylinder is smaller in size than the input cylinder
force is transmitted equally to all parts of the fluid
pressure is transmitted equally to all parts of the fluid

questions.enonce_markdown: The length of the mercury thread of a mercury-in-glass thermometer is found to be 4 cm at the lower fixed point and 19 cm at the upper fixed point. What will be the temperature of a substance in contact with the thermometer if the length of the mercury thread is now 10 cm?
questions.corrige_markdown: The fixed points are $0\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $100\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. $\theta = \dfrac{l_\theta - l_0}{l_{100} - l_0} \times 100 = \dfrac{10 - 4}{19 - 4} \times 100 = \dfrac{6}{15} \times 100 = 40\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. A common slip is to forget to subtract the length at the lower fixed point ($10/19 \times 100 \approx 53$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When spirit (volatile liquid) is dropped on the hand, the spot feels cold because:
questions.corrige_markdown: A volatile liquid evaporates quickly. To change from liquid to vapour the spirit needs latent heat of vaporization, which it takes from its surroundings, mainly the skin it touches. The hand loses heat, so the spot feels cold. The hand does not absorb the latent heat (B and D): the liquid does. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: spirit absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the hand
hand absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the spirit
spirit absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the air
hand absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the air

questions.enonce_markdown: The process of adding a controlled amount of a new element to a pure semiconductor is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Doping means adding a very small, controlled amount of an impurity (for example phosphorus or boron added to silicon) to a pure semiconductor to increase its conductivity and make n-type or p-type material. Induction is charging or generating a voltage without contact, rectification is changing a.c. to d.c., and transmutation is the change of one element into another by nuclear reaction. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A charged perspex rod brought near a small pith ball suspended on a piece of cotton thread repels the ball as shown in figure 1.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

We can conclude that the charge on the perspex rod and the pith ball are respectively:

*Options as printed:* A) negative and negative   B) negative and neutral   C) positive and positive   D) positive and neutral
questions.corrige_markdown:
Only like charges repel; a charged object attracts a neutral object. Since the ball is repelled, the ball carries a charge and it is of the same sign as the charge on the rod, which eliminates B and D (a neutral ball would be attracted). The two remaining options are 'negative and negative' and 'positive and positive'. The sign is not given in the question: by the usual textbook convention (perspex rubbed with a cloth becomes positive) the answer is positive and positive.

**Intended answer: C (positive and positive).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 2 shows how the count rate (y) of a radioactive element changes with time (t)?

![fig-2](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The count rate is proportional to the activity of the sample. It is greatest at $t = 0$ and falls exponentially: it drops by half in each half-life, quickly at first and then more and more slowly, approaching zero but never reaching it. Graph A shows this curve starting on the vertical axis at $t = 0$. Graphs B and D rise, so they are wrong. Graph C also falls but starts at a later time (it does not begin on the vertical axis), so it does not show the count rate from $t = 0$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An image formed on a screen is three times the size of the object. If the image distance is $60\ cm$, the object distance is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Linear magnification $m = \dfrac{\text{image size}}{\text{object size}} = \dfrac{v}{u}$. With $m = 3$ and $v = 60\ \mathrm{cm}$: $u = \dfrac{v}{m} = \dfrac{60}{3} = 20\ \mathrm{cm}$ (the image is real, since it is formed on a screen, and the lens formula gives $f = 15\ \mathrm{cm}$, which is consistent). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A girl stands a certain distance from a large wall and claps two blocks of wood. The echo is received 4 s later. If the speed of sound in air is $320\ m\,s^{-1}$, the distance between the girl and the wall is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The sound travels to the wall and back, so the total distance is $2d = v t = 320 \times 4 = 1280\ \mathrm{m}$, and $d = \dfrac{1280}{2} = 640\ \mathrm{m}$. The value 1280 m (option D) forgets that the sound covers the distance twice. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The graph in figure 3 is a heating curve for a substance starting from the solid state.

![fig-3](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

At which part of the curve is the substance boiling? Between:
questions.corrige_markdown: On a heating curve the temperature rises while the substance is heating in one state, and stays constant while it changes state. A to B: solid warming. B to C: first plateau, melting (solid and liquid). C to D: liquid warming. D to E: second plateau at the higher temperature, boiling (liquid and gas). So boiling takes place between D and E. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Assuming that the acceleration of free fall, g, is $10\ m\,s^{-2}$, the work done in lifting a carton of books of mass 5 kg onto a shelve 1.2 m high is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Work done $= mgh = 5 \times 10 \times 1.2 = 60\ \mathrm{J}$. Option A ($5 \times 1.2$) forgets $g$. Options B and D would need other values of $g$ or extra terms, which the question does not give. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The force acting downward from the centre of gravity of a body is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The weight of a body is the gravitational force of the Earth on it. It acts vertically downwards and is taken to act at the centre of gravity. Friction acts along a surface, the normal reaction acts perpendicular to a surface (upwards on a body resting on the ground) and tension acts along a string or rope. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 4 best represents a displacement (y) against time (t) graph for a body moving with a uniform velocity?

![fig-4](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: Uniform (constant) velocity means equal displacements in equal times, so displacement is proportional to time: $s = vt$. The graph is a straight line through the origin whose gradient is the velocity. Graph A is a horizontal line (the body is at rest), B falls steeply and flattens, and D is a curve of increasing gradient (the velocity is increasing, so the body is accelerating). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 12 m. Assuming that the acceleration of free fall, g is $10\ m\,s^{-2}$. The potential energy of the ball at that height is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Gravitational potential energy $= mgh = 0.5 \times 10 \times 12 = 60\ \mathrm{J}$. Option A ($0.5 \times 12$) forgets $g$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A worker on a site uses a pulley to lift a load to the top floor of a building. If he pulls the rope by 12 m, by how much will the load be lifted given that the velocity ratio of the pulley is 4?
questions.corrige_markdown: Velocity ratio $= \dfrac{\text{distance moved by the effort}}{\text{distance moved by the load}}$, so the load moves $\dfrac{12}{4} = 3\ \mathrm{m}$. Option A multiplies instead of dividing. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An object of mass 1.5 kg has a specific heat capacity of $450\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. What quantity of energy is needed to raise its temperature from $23\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $43\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$?
questions.corrige_markdown: $Q = mc\Delta\theta$ with $\Delta\theta = 43 - 23 = 20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C} = 20\ \mathrm{K}$ (a change of 1 K equals a change of 1 $^\circ\mathrm{C}$): $Q = 1.5 \times 450 \times 20 = 13\,500\ \mathrm{J}$. Option A uses $\Delta\theta = 2$ and option B ignores the mass and the specific heat capacity. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following can be done to increase the strength of an electromagnet?
questions.corrige_markdown: The strength of an electromagnet increases with the current, with the number of turns of the coil and with a soft-iron core. So increasing the number of turns makes it stronger. Reducing the current weakens it, thinner wires have more resistance (so less current for the same voltage), and switching the current on and off does not make it stronger. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Increase the number of turns of the coil
Continuously switch the current on and off

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following graphs in figure 5 shows how the acceleration (a) of a car varies with the force (F) of the engine?

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: By Newton's second law, $F = ma$, so $a = \dfrac{F}{m}$: for a constant mass the acceleration is directly proportional to the force. The graph of $a$ against $F$ is a straight line through the origin (graph A). Graph B is a decreasing line, C is an inverse relation and D is a curve of increasing slope. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following statements is true about a step down transformer?
questions.corrige_markdown: For a transformer $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$. A step-down transformer lowers the voltage, so $V_s < V_p$ and therefore $N_s < N_p$: the secondary coil has fewer turns than the primary. A and B describe a step-up transformer. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: It has more secondary turns than primary
It has less secondary turns than primary

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 6 shows the flux pattern of two bar magnets with poles, X and Y.

![fig-6](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

The poles X and Y are
questions.corrige_markdown: Magnetic field lines point away from a north pole and towards a south pole, and they run straight across the gap between unlike poles. In figure 6 every arrow, both in the gap and on the outer loops, points from X towards Y. So the lines leave X (a north pole) and enter Y (a south pole). If the poles were alike, the lines would repel and bend away from each other, with no line joining them. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: X: North pole and Y: North pole
X: South pole and Y: South pole
X: South pole and Y: North pole
X: North pole and Y: South pole

questions.enonce_markdown: A girl stands 3 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is she from her image?
questions.corrige_markdown: In a plane mirror the image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it. The image is 3 m behind the mirror, so the distance between the girl and her image is $3 + 3 = 6$ m. Option B gives only the image distance behind the mirror. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Below are four nuclides. $^{235}_{92}W$, $^{231}_{90}X$, $^{24}_{11}Y$, $^{238}_{92}Z$. Which pair are isotopes?
questions.corrige_markdown: Isotopes are atoms of the same element: same proton number (lower number) but different nucleon number (upper number). W has $Z = 92$ and $A = 235$; Z has $Z = 92$ and $A = 238$. Both have 92 protons but 143 and 146 neutrons respectively, so W and Z are isotopes (uranium-235 and uranium-238). X has 90 protons and Y has 11, so neither pairs with another nuclide. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 7 shows a displacement-time graph of a single particle in a wave.

![fig-7](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)

The interval, X, represents the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The graph shows the displacement of one particle against time, so the horizontal axis is time. The interval X starts at the origin and ends when the particle is back at the same displacement moving in the same direction: one complete oscillation. The time for one complete oscillation is the period. Wavelength would be read on a displacement-distance graph, and frequency (a number per second) is not a time interval. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the contact force in the list of forces below.
questions.corrige_markdown: A contact force acts only when two bodies touch. Upthrust is the force of a fluid on an object immersed in it, so the fluid and the object are in contact. Weight (gravitational), magnetic and electrostatic forces act at a distance, through a field. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The loudness of a sound wave depends on:
questions.corrige_markdown: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the wave: a larger amplitude carries more energy and sounds louder. Frequency determines the pitch. Wavelength and velocity do not determine loudness. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The activity of a radio-isotope is 640 counts per minute. Two hours later, it falls to 160 counts per minute. The half-life of the sample is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $640 \to 320 \to 160$: the activity is halved twice, so 2 hours is two half-lives. Half-life $= \dfrac{2\ \mathrm{h}}{2} = 1\ \mathrm{hour}$. Option B would be one half-life, but the activity has fallen to a quarter, not a half. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT an application of electrostatics?
questions.corrige_markdown: Spray painting (charged paint droplets attracted to the object), dust removal in chimneys (electrostatic precipitator) and photocopying (charged drum attracting toner) all use static charges. The electricity supply at home is a flowing current (current electricity), not static charge. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Sound waves are heard around corners because they can be easily:
questions.corrige_markdown: Diffraction is the spreading of a wave when it passes an opening or goes round an obstacle, and it is strongest when the size of the gap is about the same as the wavelength. Sound has a long wavelength (centimetres to metres), comparable with doors and corners, so it diffracts round corners and can be heard there. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following forces increases with an increase in the speed of an object?
questions.corrige_markdown: Drag (air or fluid resistance) grows as the speed of the object through the fluid increases. The electrostatic force depends on the charges and their separation, the gravitational force on the masses and their separation, and upthrust on the weight of fluid displaced. None of these depends on speed. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The functioning of a spring balance is an application of:
questions.corrige_markdown: A spring balance relies on the extension of a spring being proportional to the load (force) applied, as long as the elastic limit is not passed: this is Hooke's law, $F = ke$, and it is why the scale is evenly spaced. Lenz's law is about induced currents and Ohm's law about current and voltage. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the particle $^{a}_{b}X$ emitted in this radioactive decay process: $^{238}_{92}U \to {}^{234}_{90}Th + {}^{a}_{b}X$
questions.corrige_markdown: Conservation of nucleon number: $238 = 234 + a$, so $a = 4$. Conservation of proton number (charge): $92 = 90 + b$, so $b = 2$. A particle with 4 nucleons and 2 protons is a helium nucleus, an alpha particle, $^{4}_{2}He$. Option D has the numbers the wrong way round. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the number of electrons in a polythene rod when it is charged with 54000 C. ($e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\ C$)
questions.corrige_markdown: The charge is a whole number of electron charges: $n = \dfrac{Q}{e} = \dfrac{54000}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} = 3.375 \times 10^{23} \approx 3.38 \times 10^{23}$ electrons. Option A multiplies $Q$ and $e$ instead of dividing, and C and D use the wrong power of ten. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A disease in the thyroid gland of a woman is treated using a radioactive iodine-131 labeled salt. Which device could be used to monitor the progress of the salt in-take?
questions.corrige_markdown: Iodine-131 emits radiation, so the radiation emitted by the labelled salt (the tracer) is detected outside the body with a Geiger-Muller tube (counter), which shows where the iodine has gone and how much has been taken up. A manometer measures pressure, a thermometer temperature and a cathode ray oscilloscope displays voltage signals. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A wave of frequency of $50\ Hz$ is moving with speed of $10\ m\,s^{-1}$. The wavelength of is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $v = f\lambda$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{10}{50} = 0.2\ \mathrm{m}$. Option D inverts the fraction ($f \div v = 5$). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A liquid of mass 30 g has a density of $4\ g\,cm^{-3}$. Its volume is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Density $\rho = \dfrac{m}{V}$, so $V = \dfrac{m}{\rho} = \dfrac{30\ \mathrm{g}}{4\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}} = 7.5\ \mathrm{cm^3}$. Option A multiplies mass and density instead of dividing. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the longest wavelength?
questions.corrige_markdown: In order of increasing wavelength the electromagnetic spectrum runs: gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, radio waves. Radio waves have the longest wavelength (and the lowest frequency) of the four options. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 43 - 46

Figure 8 shows a setup used for measuring the acceleration due to gravity.

![fig-8](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)

The ball could be made of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The ball is held by an electromagnet before it is released, so it must be attracted by a magnet: it has to be made of a magnetic material such as iron or steel. Polythene, glass and copper are not magnetic, so the electromagnet could not hold them. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The ball is dropped by:
questions.corrige_markdown: The electromagnet holds the steel ball only while the current flows. Switching the current off removes the magnetic force, so the ball is released and falls freely. Switching the electromagnet on would hold the ball, and the light sensors only detect the ball passing and start and stop the timer. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The equation used to analyse the data collected from this experiment is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The timer gives the time $t$ taken by the ball to fall the measured height $h = s$ between the light sensors. The ball is released from rest by the electromagnet just above the upper sensor, so $u \approx 0$ and $a = g$: $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ becomes $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$, so $g = \dfrac{2h}{t^2}$. This is the only equation that uses the quantities measured in the experiment, the distance and the time (the other three need a velocity, which is not measured). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Air resistance has little effect on the results obtained because the ball is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Air resistance matters when the object has a large surface area, a low weight and a high speed. A small, heavy ball has a small area compared with its weight, and falling only a short distance it does not reach a high speed. So air resistance is small compared with its weight and the acceleration stays very close to $g$. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: small, heavy and falls only a short distance
small, heavy and falls a long distance
small, lightweight and falls only a short distance
big, lightweight and falls a long distance

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 47 - 50

The set up in figure 9 is used by a student to investigate the relationship between the current, I, flowing through a conductor of resistance, R, and the potential difference across its ends, V.

![fig-9](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_9.png)

Which law in physics is under investigation?
questions.corrige_markdown: The circuit measures the current through a conductor (ammeter) and the potential difference across it (voltmeter), changing the current with a variable resistor. The relationship between V and I for a conductor is Ohm's law: $V = IR$, with $V$ proportional to $I$ at constant temperature. Hooke's law concerns springs, and Faraday's and Lenz's laws concern electromagnetic induction. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is component X?
questions.corrige_markdown: Component X is drawn as a resistor with an arrow through it, which is the symbol of a variable resistor (rheostat). It is used to change the current in the circuit. The ammeter and the voltmeter are drawn as circles with A and V, and the fixed resistor R is drawn without an arrow. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What property of meter A, permits it to be connected as shown?
questions.corrige_markdown: Meter A is an ammeter, connected in series with the conductor. It must have a very low resistance so that it does not change the current it is measuring. (A voltmeter, connected in parallel, is the one with a very high resistance.) **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
If the conductor is a wire, which of the following graphs in figure 10 represents the shape of a graph of V against I?

![fig-10](gce-ol-physics-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_10.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: A metallic wire at constant temperature obeys Ohm's law, $V = IR$, so $V$ is proportional to $I$: the graph is a straight line through the origin whose gradient is the resistance $R$ (graph D). Graph A is a decreasing line, B is a curve with increasing slope (a non-ohmic conductor such as a lamp filament) and C is an inverse curve. **Answer: D.**
